title: सितारे क्यों झिलमिलाते हैं? विज्ञान में छुपा रहस्य
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer about why stars appear to twinkle while planets look steady. The hook must be a one‑breath question like “Ever wondered why stars sparkle but planets don’t?” Use stock footage of night skies, close‑ups of stars, planet imagery, and atmospheric visuals (clouds, wind). Explain the surprising angle: tiny temperature‑driven air currents bend starlight, causing rapid flicker; planets are closer and appear as discs, so the effect averages out. No charts or heavy jargon needed.

title: बिल्ली हमेशा पैर पर क्यों उतरती है? विज्ञान का रहस्य
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical short that explains why cats can twist mid‑air and always land on their feet. Use stock footage of cats jumping, falling, and landing (including slow‑motion clips), plus any generic close‑up shots of a cat's spine or whiskers to illustrate the righting reflex. Keep the narration clear, wonder‑filled, and in Hindi, emphasizing the curiosity gap: why does this happen?

title: आइस्क्रीम खाने पर अचानक दिमाग में तेज़ दर्द क्यों होता है?
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer about why a sudden "brain freeze" (ice‑cream headache) happens when you eat something cold too quickly. Open with a one‑breath hook that asks viewers if they’ve ever felt that sharp pain in their head after a quick lick of ice‑cream. Explain the nerve‑signal mix‑up between the mouth and brain, using stock footage of ice‑cream, someone eating it fast, close‑up of a tongue, and visual metaphors of nerves flashing, plus a quick cut to a brain diagram (static image) to illustrate the pain signal. Keep language simple, no charts, no jargon.

title: ट्रेन के ब्रेक की चिल्लाहट क्यों सुनते हैं? विज्ञान का रहस्य
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer using only stock footage of trains, tracks, brake systems, and visualizations of vibrations. Narrate in Hindi, starting with a hook that makes viewers wonder why trains emit that loud, high‑pitched squeal when they brake. Explain the physics: friction between brake pads and wheels creates rapid vibration, the metal surfaces resonate, and the sound serves as a safety cue. Keep language simple, avoid technical jargon, and end with a quick recap.

title: टोस्ट हमेशा मक्खन वाली साइड नीचे क्यों गिरता है? | फ़िज़िक्स का रहस्य
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer about why a piece of toast almost always lands butter‑side down when it falls. Highlight the surprising physics: the offset center of mass, the typical drop height causing a half‑rotation, and the role of butter spreading. Open with the hook: “Ever wonder why your toast always lands butter‑side down?” Use only stock footage of toast being sliced, buttered, dropped, slow‑motion flip, kitchen surfaces, and a hand catching it.

title: सुनते ही गूज़बम्प क्यों बनते हैं? आपका शरीर डर से क्यों कांपता है!
prompt: Create a 45-60 second faceless explainer about the sudden goosebumps (piloerection) people get when they hear a scary sound. Start with the hook: "Why does your skin literally stand up when you hear a scary sound?" Use stock footage of people reacting to sudden loud/shriek sounds, close‑up shots of skin where goosebumps appear, animals (cats, dogs) with fur standing on end, and a quick montage of ancient humans in fur coats. Explain the surprising angle: it's a vestigial reflex from our hairy ancestors that made us look bigger and trapped warm air to keep us warm, now triggered by emotional arousal. Keep narration simple, no jargon, in Hindi.

title: सूर्योदय‑सूर्यास्त में आकाश लाल क्यों होता है? जानिए विज्ञान का राज
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer about why the sky turns red during sunrise and sunset. Open with a one‑breath hook that asks the viewer why the horizon glows crimson. Use only stock footage of dawn/dusk skies, sun rays, clouds, simple lab‑style light scattering demos, and close‑up of the sun’s edge. Script should explain in Hindi how longer atmospheric path scatters blue light, leaving red wavelengths, without needing diagrams or jargon.

title: फ्रीज़र में बोतल रखी तो क्यों फट जाती है? विज्ञान का रहस्य
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer using stock footage that shows a glass bottle being placed in a freezer, the ice forming inside, and the bottle shattering when removed. Open with a hook that asks why a simple bottle can explode in the freezer, then explain the physics of water expansion, pressure buildup, and glass strength in simple Hindi narration. Use clear, close‑up shots of the bottle, freezer door, and the break‑apart moment; no on‑screen text needed.

title: कुत्ते क्यों झुका रहे हैं सिर? विज्ञान से जानिए चुटीला कारण!
prompt: Create a 45-60 second vertical explainer using only stock footage and photos. Topic: why dogs tilt their heads when you talk. Surprising angle: it's not just cuteness, it's a clever adaptation to better locate sounds and interpret human facial cues. Hook to open with in one breath: "Ever wonder why dogs tilt their heads every time you speak?"

title: चार्ज पर फोन इस्तेमाल करने से बैटरी क्यों जल्दी ख़त्म हो जाती है? जानिए कारण
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer using only stock footage of smartphones, charging cables, batteries, heat visuals, and close‑ups of battery indicators. Topic: Why does a phone’s battery drain faster when you use it while it’s charging? The surprising angle: the hidden heat and voltage stress that actually harms the battery, not just the power draw. Opening hook (one breath): "क्या आपने कभी सोचा है कि चार्ज करते‑समय फोन इस्तेमाल करने से बैटरी जल्दी ख़त्म क्यों हो जाती है?" The narration should explain in simple Hindi the concepts of heat buildup, voltage spikes, and chemical stress, ending with a practical tip to avoid this.
